quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results (CFO Sinead Gorman): adjusted earnings of $9.8 billion and over $21 billion of cash flow from operations despite the ongoing disruptions in the Middle East; free cash flow of 'some $17 billion in one quarter'. LNG trading and optimization captured significant additional value versus the prior quarter. Chemicals made a positive free cash flow contribution and the CFO called the quarter's chemicals results 'the best we have seen in over five years', weighted more toward cost take-out and asset operating performance than margins (the Monaca, Pennsylvania complex hit record performance). Refineries achieved a record 102% utilization, shifting output toward middle distillates such as jet fuel; Brazil delivered another quarter of record production. Net debt was reduced to some $42 billion, or $12 billion excluding leases.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted earnings $9.8 billion; cash flow from operations over $21 billion; refinery utilization 102%; net debt some $42 billion ($12 billion excluding leases)

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook: the 2026 cash capex outlook of $24 billion-$26 billion is unchanged (raised from $20 billion-$22 billion per year when the ARC Resources transaction was agreed; it includes some $4 billion for the ARC acquisition and associated cash capex). CFO: the company is confident of delivering within the range; it sees inflation in the system of around 5%-6% overall, largely offset through scale, framework agreements and early lock-ins, and rigs are less of a problem because they were locked in in advance (CEO: 'in particular, those deep water rigs'). Q3 (CFO): a positive refining margin environment but softening chemical spreads, somewhat more downstream turnarounds than in Q2, less volatility and so a little less trading contribution in downstream, and a more challenging lubricants quarter because Pearl GTL volumes are not expected in the near term. CEO: trading and supply's 2%-4% ROACE uplift continues to hold; it is at the top end of that range and, if volatility continues into Q3, is expected to stay in a healthy part of the range.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 cash capex $24 billion-$26 billion (unchanged), incl. some $4 billion for ARC; inflation around 5%-6%; trading and supply 2%-4% ROACE uplift

quarterly_data.signal: Middle East disruption and supply: Shell lost LNG volumes from Qatar (CEO: Qatar is a critical part of the LNG mix with 20% of the volumes; CFO: some 25 million tonnes or more taken out of the market by events in the Strait) but kept roughly the same LNG output by drawing more volumes from Nigeria and Trinidad, LNG Canada (more than 100 cargoes since its first cargo a year ago and full capacity this quarter) and near-record third-party volumes, including buying back some of its own sold cargoes to redirect them. Pearl GTL: the train not impacted by the hostilities could be back up and running within weeks once access and safe passage allow; repairs to the damaged second train are expected to be complete by end of Q1 2027, subject to the ability to export. CFO: cargoes are being redirected from Asia to Europe, where storage is closer to 50%, which 'does make for a tightness coming in the next quarter or so'.
quarterly_data.figure: Qatar 20% of LNG volumes; some 25 million tonnes or more out of the market; LNG Canada more than 100 cargoes; Pearl GTL train two back by end of Q1 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Project pipeline and dates (CEO Wael Sawan): the ARC Resources acquisition won overwhelming shareholder support and is expected to close in Q3, depending on the last approval under the Investment Canada Act. LNG Canada Phase 2 FID is targeted before the end of this year with the joint-venture partners, subject to approvals; Bonga South West FID hoped for in 2027 and Zabazaba around 2027, 2028; in Venezuela, the Dragon project is aimed at an FID at some point in 2027, Shell signed contracts to operate the offshore Loran gas field and was granted the licence for Loran Phase One (a 1.7 TCF opportunity that could tie back into Atlantic LNG), leveraging the Manatee development that starts up in the next 12 to 18 months. In Namibia Shell drilled its most promising exploration well to date and is expediting two appraisal wells to the end of this year; a well offshore Egypt proved a working petroleum system, but commerciality is too early to call.
quarterly_data.figure: ARC close expected Q3; LNG Canada Phase 2 FID targeted before end of this year; Bonga South West FID 2027; Loran Phase One 1.7 TCF; Manatee start-up in the next 12 to 18 months

quarterly_data.signal: Growth and free cash flow framework (CEO): the ARC Resources deal sustains material liquids production and grows integrated gas, lifting Shell's expected production growth to 2030 from around 1% a year to some 4% compared with 2025, and is expected to add roughly $1.5 billion per year of free cash flow once completed; ARC gas underwrites enough feedstock for a second LNG Canada phase, which was not in the deal's base economics. The CEO sees line of sight to double-digit returns on ARC. Base free cash flow has been roughly $25 billion-$30 billion per year on a $70 real-term basis; the CEO says the 2030 period is fully de-risked and Shell is well on its way towards 2035, with LNG Canada Phase 2 (if sanctioned) adding the next layer of free cash flow in the 2030s. On M&A, nothing seen so far comes close to ARC, and the CEO calls oil 'more of a seller's market'.
quarterly_data.figure: production growth to 2030 from around 1% a year to some 4%; ARC adds roughly $1.5 billion per year free cash flow; base free cash flow $25 billion-$30 billion per year

quarterly_data.signal: Costs and portfolio (CEO): structural cost reductions of $700 million delivered so far in 2026; high-grading of the portfolio has delivered savings of close to $6 billion since 2022, about halfway through the $5 billion to $7 billion target band, and the CEO is pushing the teams to reach the top end and to use AI to unlock more value. Divestments: the non-operated working interest in Na Kika (Gulf of Mexico), Sprng Energy in India (power portfolio), the completed sale of the U.S. Jiffy Lube network and the South African mobility sites. On the $45 billion of underperforming capital employed, low-carbon capital such as CCS and Holland Hydrogen 1 in Rotterdam is expected to start showing a return likely from 2027, with a return north of 10% expected on that business before the end of the decade. At Norco, traders now work alongside operators on feedstock and product placement (jet versus diesel and gasoline), a model being rolled out to every refinery; the CFO says trading has never lost money in any quarter in the last decade.
quarterly_data.figure: $700 million structural cost reductions in 2026; close to $6 billion savings since 2022 vs $5 billion to $7 billion target; low-carbon return north of 10% before end of decade

quarterly_data.signal: LNG outlook (CEO): Shell reaffirmed its long-term conviction of 65% growth in the LNG market between now and 2050 and anticipates around 180 million tons of new annual supply coming into the market by 2030, so term markets should remain well supplied; demand growth is coming from transportation (more than predicted a few years ago), the adjacency to power and renewables, Southeast Asian countries with maturing indigenous gas fields, and Europe. Shell holds roughly 10% of overall production in Brazil, where the CEO is encouraged by the subsurface and Petrobras' operation of the Tupi, Iracema and Mero fields.
quarterly_data.figure: 65% LNG market growth to 2050; around 180 million tons of new annual supply by 2030; roughly 10% of Brazil's production
